texts.label: text
texts.orig: Whenever the product is subsequently put into operation ensure that:
texts.text: Whenever the product is subsequently put into operation ensure that:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · All personnel is clear of the danger zone surrounding moving parts of the machine. Electrically-actuated linkages may be set in motion when the Engine Control Unit (governor) is switched on.
texts.text: All personnel is clear of the danger zone surrounding moving parts of the machine. Electrically-actuated linkages may be set in motion when the Engine Control Unit (governor) is switched on.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · All maintenance and repair work has been completed.
texts.text: All maintenance and repair work has been completed.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · All loose parts have been removed from rotating machine components.
texts.text: All loose parts have been removed from rotating machine components.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · All protective devices are in place.
texts.text: All protective devices are in place.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · All lines bearing media are ready for operation.
texts.text: All lines bearing media are ready for operation.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: The walkways in the operating room are unobstructed and safe.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: The exhaust pipework is leak-tight and the gases are vented to atmosphere.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: The product is entirely free of damage, this applies in particular to lines and cabling.

texts.text: Battery terminals, generator terminals or cables are protected against accidental contact.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The engine oil circuit is equipped with an automatic oil replenishment system. During engine operation, the oil level in the engine oil pan is compensated (filled) continuously from the replenishment tank. In normal engine operation, the engine oil level is therefore only checked or topped up in the replenishment tank.
texts.text: The engine oil circuit is equipped with an automatic oil replenishment system. During engine operation, the oil level in the engine oil pan is compensated (filled) continuously from the replenishment tank. texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 5. Unscrew nuts (3) with washers (4) from threa‐ ded pin (2).
texts.text: Unscrew nuts (3) with washers (4) from threa‐ ded pin (2).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 6. Remove threaded pin (2) from resilient mount.
texts.text: Remove threaded pin (2) from resilient mount.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 8. Screw studs (8) into base plate of resilient mount.
texts.text: Screw studs (8) into base plate of resilient mount.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 9. Screw on nuts (5) together with washers (6) and fix studs (8) with locknut.
texts.text: Screw on nuts (5) together with washers (6) and fix studs (8) with locknut.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 10. Screw on nuts (7) and fit washers (9).
texts.text: Screw on nuts (7) and fit washers (9).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 11. Mount locking parts (10) and (2) screw on nuts (3) with washers (4) until they make con‐ tact with the locking part (2).
texts.text: Mount locking parts (10) and (2) screw on nuts (3) with washers (4) until they make con‐ tact with the locking part (2).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 12. Screw nuts (7) from below against blocking parts (10) and (2) and tighten them.
texts.text: Screw nuts (7) from below against blocking parts (10) and (2) and tighten them.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Result: Resilient mount is secured against compressi‐ on and the height dimension is retained.
texts.text: Result: Resilient mount is secured against compressi‐ on and the height dimension is retained.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Loosen adjusting screw (1) a few rotations to guarantee ease of movement between resili‐ ent mount and adjusting screw (1).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 14. Remove locked resilient mount with suitable lifting gear between base frame and engine mounting bracket.
texts.text: Remove locked resilient mount with suitable lifting gear between base frame and engine mounting bracket.

texts.orig: 1. Attach engine mounting bracket (1) to crane with a lightly tensioned rope.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Note: Remove engine support only if necessary. Ensure that supports are not stressed by engine.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Remove screws and washers on engine support.
texts.text: Remove screws and washers on engine support.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Insert screws (1) with washers of engine mounting brackets on driving end and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.
texts.text: Insert screws (1) with washers of engine mounting brackets on driving end and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.

texts.text: There must not be any gap between the engine support mating face and the equipment carrier.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 2. Insert screws (4) with washers of engine mounting brackets on free end and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.
texts.text: Insert screws (4) with washers of engine mounting brackets on free end and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.

texts.label: text

texts.text: Engine operation is only allowed with unloaded engine mounting bracket!

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3. Set screws (2) and (5) to dimension (A = 80 to 85 mm, B = 40 to 45 mm) and tighten nut (3) to specified tightening torque.
texts.text: Set screws (2) and (5) to dimension (A = 80 to 85 mm, B = 40 to 45 mm) and tighten nut (3) to specified tightening torque.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Coat O-ring with assembly compound and in‐ sert in groove on engine mounting bracket (1) as per overview drawing (→ Page 544) .

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3. Position engine mounting bracket (1) with ro‐ pe and crane at crankcase.
texts.text: Position engine mounting bracket (1) with ro‐ pe and crane at crankcase.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 5. Insert screws (3) with washers (2) and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.
texts.text: Insert screws (3) with washers (2) and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Install locking device (2) with studs, nuts and washers as shown on new resilient mount.
texts.text: Install locking device (2) with studs, nuts and washers as shown on new resilient mount.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 2. Set height dimension (1) at new resilient mount with locking device (2) to measured va‐ lue of the resilient mount to be replaced.
texts.text: Set height dimension (1) at new resilient mount with locking device (2) to measured va‐ lue of the resilient mount to be replaced.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3. Clean and degrease flange-mounting surfa‐ ces of resilient mount, foundation, and adjus‐ ting screw.
texts.text: Clean and degrease flange-mounting surfa‐ ces of resilient mount, foundation, and adjus‐ ting screw.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 4. Use suitable lifting equipment to insert locked resilient mount (4) between foundation and engine mounting bracket and align it to the bores in the foundation.
texts.text: Use suitable lifting equipment to insert locked resilient mount (4) between foundation and engine mounting bracket and align it to the bores in the foundation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 7. Coat threaded pins (1) with engine oil.
texts.text: Coat threaded pins (1) with engine oil.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 8. Insert threaded pin (1) into resilient mount and use torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.
texts.text: Insert threaded pin (1) into resilient mount and use torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 9. Screw in adjusting screw (1) as far as the stop on resilient mount.
texts.text: Screw in adjusting screw (1) as far as the stop on resilient mount.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 10. Screw on nuts (2) with washers (3) and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.
texts.text: Screw on nuts (2) with washers (3) and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 11. Release upper nuts on locking device (6) alternately and evenly.
texts.text: Release upper nuts on locking device (6) alternately and evenly.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 12. Remove locking device (6) with studs, nuts and washers from resilient mount.
texts.text: Remove locking device (6) with studs, nuts and washers from resilient mount.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 13. Install screws (4) with washers (5) and use a torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.
texts.text: Install screws (4) with washers (5) and use a torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 14. Release nut (7) and back off screw (8) on all engine supports (9) until there is sufficient clearance to the foun‐ dation.
texts.text: Release nut (7) and back off screw (8) on all engine supports (9) until there is sufficient clearance to the foun‐ dation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 15. Lock screw (8) with nut (7) on all engine supports (9) with locknut.
texts.text: Lock screw (8) with nut (7) on all engine supports (9) with locknut.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Install engine coolant pump, if engine mounting was removed on left engine side, free end (→ Page 480) .
texts.text: Install engine coolant pump, if engine mounting was removed on left engine side, free end (→ Page 480) .

table_cells.text: Minor dirt scores can occur during the assembly of a new engine (honing products, particles, broken-off burrs). Removed cylinders clearly show such scoring on the running surface under endoscope magnification. Cannot be felt with the fingernail. Findings not critical
Clearly visible scores caused by hard particles. They usually start in the TDC area and cross through the honing pattern in the direction of stroke. Findings not critical

These areas consist of scores of different length and depth next to one another. In most cases, they are found at the 6-o'clock and 12-o'clock positions (inlet/exhaust) along the transverse engine axis. Findings not critical

Polished areas are on the running surface but almost the whole honing pattern is still visible. Polished areas appear brighter and more shiny than the surrounding running surface. Findings not critical
Bright areas are on the running surface and show local removal of the honing pat‐ tern. Grooves from the honing process are not visible any more.

This is caused by oxidation (surface discoloration through oil or fuel) and temperatu‐ re differences around the liner. It appears rather darker within the honed structure in contrast to the bright metallic running surface. The honing pattern is undisturbed. Discolorations extend in stroke direction and may be interrupted. Findings not critical

Corrosion fields / spots result from moisture (condensate) with the valves in the overlap (open) position. They are clearly visible due to the dark color of the honing groove bottom. This corrosion is not critical unless there is corrosion pitting.

Black lines are a preliminary stage of burn marks. They are visible as a clear disco‐ loration from TDC to BDC in the running surface and the start of localized damage to the honing pattern. Cylinder liners with a large number of black lines around the running surface have limited service life and should be replaced.

These are caused by a disturbance in the liner / ring tribo system. Usually they run over the whole ring-travel area (TDC/BDC), starting at the first TDC-ring and beco‐ ming more visible from the second TDC-ring 2 onwards and less pronounced from TDC-ring 1. The honing pattern is usually no longer visible and displays a clearly defined (straight) edge to the undisturbed surface. The damaged surface is usually discolored. The circumferential length varies. Liners with burn marks starting in TDC ring 1 have to be replaced.

Irregular circumference lengths and depths. Can be caused either by the piston skirt or the piston crown. Material deposits on the liner (smears), heavy discoloration. Se‐ vere, visible scoring. Replace liner.
Cylinder liner wear in TDC area
Cylinder liner wear in the TDC area occurs when hydrodynamic friction between pis‐ ton rings and cylinder changes to mixed friction under maximum firing pressures.
